index.title: Java SDE-2 Interview Preparation Series Index

books.title: Java Foundations for Problem Solving
books.subtitle: Java Fundamentals for DSA and SDE-2 Interviews
books.purpose: This volume is the canonical Java language foundation and the recommended first book in the series. It starts with source-to-execution and program structure, builds through types, control flow, methods, arrays, strings, objects, core libraries, exceptions, generics, and usage-first collections, then converts that knowledge into interview-quality implementation and debugging skill.

books.title: Time and Space Complexity for Java Interviews
books.subtitle: From First Operation Counts to SDE-2 Trade-off Reasoning
books.purpose: This volume is the bridge from Java syntax to algorithmic problem solving. It begins with concrete operation counts, introduces growth and space gently, then develops the qualified cost models, constraints, invariants, amortization, and optimization explanations expected in SDE-2 interviews.

books.title: Number Systems and Math Foundations for DSA Interviews
books.subtitle: Part A: The Practical Numeric Foundation for Java Coding Interviews
books.purpose: This volume closes the mathematical prerequisite gap before bit manipulation, arrays, binary search, hashing, and number-based coding problems. It is practical DSA mathematics, not an academic number-theory textbook.

books.title: Number Systems Interview Patterns and Rapid Revision
books.subtitle: Part B: Fifty-Two Implementations, Java Traps, Exercises, Solutions, and Readiness
books.purpose: This linked workbook completes Stage 1 with the 52-implementation catalog, Java number traps, conceptual and code-output questions, debugging tasks, coding exercises, solutions, follow-up chains, cheat sheet, and readiness assessment.

books.title: Bit Manipulation in Java
books.subtitle: From First Bits to SDE-2 Interview Techniques
books.purpose: This dedicated volume turns the binary foundation from Volume 01 into a progressive Java interview toolkit. It begins with visible bit patterns and safe operators, derives each shortcut instead of asking readers to memorize it, then develops XOR families, subset state, SDE-2 problem patterns, Java APIs, and production-quality bit fields.

books.title: Loop Mastery, Patterns, and Index Calculations
books.subtitle: From Your First Loop to SDE-2 Index Reasoning
books.purpose: This volume is the bridge from basic Java control flow to reliable array and string problem solving. It begins with the execution model of for, while, do-while, and enhanced-for loops; builds a visual language for ranges and invariants; then derives pointer, compaction, window, search, and matrix patterns without asking the reader to memorize templates blindly.

books.title: Arrays and Array Problem-Solving Patterns
books.subtitle: Traversal, In-Place Work, Pointers, Windows, Prefix Sums, and Sorting
books.purpose: Arrays are the default interview state space. This volume joins Java representation rules with the pattern-selection reasoning needed for efficient solutions.

books.title: Strings and String Problem-Solving Patterns
books.subtitle: Unicode-Aware Traversal, Windows, Builders, Parsing, and Text Boundaries
books.purpose: String interviews mix algorithm patterns with Java-specific text semantics. This volume makes that boundary explicit so code is both efficient and correct.

books.title: Hashing: Maps, Sets, Frequency, and Prefix State
books.subtitle: Equality Contracts, Frequency Maps, Deduplication, and Expected Complexity
books.purpose: Hashing is both a DSA pattern and a Java object-contract problem. This volume connects the two so expected O(1) claims remain defensible.

books.title: Recursion and Backtracking in Java
books.subtitle: Contracts, Call Stacks, Search Trees, Pruning, and State Restoration
books.purpose: This volume separates recursion as a method contract from backtracking as controlled state-space search, with Java stack and mutation behavior made explicit.

books.title: Linked Lists: Pointer Reasoning and Mutation
books.subtitle: Nodes, Sentinels, Fast-Slow Pointers, Reversal, Cycles, and Merging
books.purpose: Linked-list problems expose whether a candidate can preserve reachability while mutating references. This volume makes those invariants visible.

books.title: Stacks, Queues, Deques, and Monotonic Patterns
books.subtitle: LIFO, FIFO, Sliding Extrema, Next-Greater State, and Java ArrayDeque
books.purpose: This volume unifies ordering data structures around the state each one preserves, then applies monotonic structures to linear-time interview patterns.

books.title: Binary Search: Bounds, Answers, and Invariants
books.subtitle: Exact Matches, Lower Bounds, Monotone Predicates, and Safe Midpoints
books.purpose: Binary search is a proof pattern over monotone state. This volume centers interval semantics, duplicates, insertion points, overflow-safe midpoint calculation, and search on answers.

books.title: Trees, Binary Search Trees, and Tries
books.subtitle: Traversal Contracts, Path State, Ordering, Balance, and Prefix Search
books.purpose: Tree interviews test recursion, state ownership, structural invariants, and the ability to translate ordering into pruning.

books.title: Heaps, Priority Queues, Selection, and Top-K
books.subtitle: Heap Invariants, Comparator Safety, K-Way Processing, and Partial Ordering
books.purpose: This volume distinguishes heap order from global sorting and develops priority-based interview patterns without hiding comparator or mutation risks.

books.title: Graphs: Traversal, Ordering, Paths, and Union-Find
books.subtitle: Modeling, BFS, DFS, Topological Sort, Shortest Paths, and Connectivity
books.purpose: Graph problems become manageable once the model and edge semantics are explicit. This volume emphasizes algorithm selection, state, overflow, and correctness.

books.title: Greedy Algorithms: Recognition, Proofs, and Scheduling
books.subtitle: Local Choices, Exchange Arguments, Counterexamples, and Interval Decisions
books.purpose: Greedy solutions are short to code and hard to justify. This volume centers the proof obligation, not the superficial loop.

books.title: Dynamic Programming: State, Transitions, and Optimization
books.subtitle: Memoization, Tabulation, Reconstruction, Dimensions, and Space Compression
books.purpose: This volume makes dynamic programming a specification process: define exactly what a state means, how it depends on smaller states, and what information can be compressed.

books.title: Advanced Java A: JVM and Execution
books.subtitle: Platform Model, Bytecode, Loading, Memory, GC, JIT, and Runtime Semantics
books.purpose: Part A builds the execution model needed to reason about Java behavior beneath syntax without presenting implementation details as language guarantees.

books.title: Advanced Java B: Language, OOP, and Modern Java
books.subtitle: Objects, Inheritance, Interfaces, Equality, Exceptions, Generics, Lambdas, and Java 21
books.purpose: Part B covers the language-engineering depth expected when SDE-2 interviews move beyond coding patterns into API design and type safety.

books.title: Advanced Java C: Collections, Streams, and I/O
books.subtitle: Collection Semantics, Ordering, Streams, NIO.2, Files, Buffers, and Boundaries
books.purpose: Part C is the advanced Java-library companion to the DSA volumes, emphasizing API contracts, representation costs, resource ownership, and production boundaries.

books.title: Advanced Java D: Concurrency and the Memory Model
books.subtitle: Threads, Happens-Before, Locks, Atomics, Executors, Virtual Threads, and Failure Modes
books.purpose: Part D develops concurrency correctness from first principles and then connects it to production scheduling, cancellation, backpressure, and testing.

books.title: Advanced Java E: Performance, Diagnostics, and GC Incidents
books.subtitle: Measurement, JMH, jcmd, JFR, Thread Dumps, Heap Evidence, and Tuning Playbooks
books.purpose: Part E teaches an evidence-first diagnostic method so performance claims and tuning actions remain falsifiable and operationally safe.

books.title: Advanced Java F: Design, Backend, Testing, and Security
books.subtitle: SOLID APIs, Patterns, Transactions, Services, Build Quality, Reliability, and Secure Boundaries
books.purpose: Part F covers the engineering judgment that distinguishes SDE-2 candidates from syntax-only candidates: boundaries, invariants, failure policy, observability, and maintainability.

books.title: Advanced Java G: Question Bank, Study Plan, and Reference
books.subtitle: Interview Questions, Mock Loops, Solutions, Glossary, References, and Final Readiness
books.purpose: Part G is the core Java revision system. It consolidates interview questions, selected solutions, study loops, terminology, and primary references without replacing deliberate practice.

books.title: Advanced Java H: Spring Boot and REST APIs
books.subtitle: Dependency Injection, MVC Contracts, Transactions, Idempotency, Operations, and Testing
books.purpose: Part H opens the backend specialist track with the Spring and HTTP reasoning expected in Java SDE-2 interviews, while keeping framework behavior tied to explicit contracts and failure modes.

books.title: Advanced Java I: Persistence, SQL, JPA, and Caching
books.subtitle: Relational Models, Indexes, Query Plans, Transactions, Hibernate, Redis, and Consistency
books.purpose: Part I develops the persistence judgment needed to design correct, measurable Java data paths instead of treating databases, ORMs, and caches as interchangeable storage APIs.

books.title: Advanced Java J: Distributed Systems and System Design
books.subtitle: Capacity, Partitioning, Consistency, Kafka, Resilience, Sagas, Observability, and SLOs
books.purpose: Part J completes the backend specialist track with a constraint-first system-design method spanning distributed data, messaging, failure control, and operations.
